results.summary: This design is a 24-voice music synthesizer for the TTSKY26a demo competition. It computes a new sample every 800 cycles and outputs audio at 31.5 kHz using PWM with delta-sigma modulation. It also generates a VGA visualization of the voices and uses a sequencer to arrange melody, bass and accompaniment. The design uses a radix-4 Booth multiplier and supports a speedup option to skip unused cycles.

results.summary: This project instantiates one copy of each standard cell from the GF180mcu 7-track library. It multiplexes the project I/O pins so that the functional behaviour of each cell can be verified. The 210 cell outputs are arranged into 27 pages of 8 pins, selected by ui_in[4:0]. The selected page's outputs appear on uo_out.

results.summary_before: This project is a naive and very simple implementation of a stream cipher demonstration. It uses a linear-feedback shift register (LFSR) to generate a pseudo-random keystream. The bidirectional pins are configured as inputs only and are never driven by the design. The cipher is intended for educational purposes and is not secure for real-world use.
results.summary: This project implements an I2C slave that emulates a real-world sensor. It exposes two register banks of eight 8-bit registers each, with Block A writable and Block B read-only and driven by an internal LFSR. The slave operates at Standard, Fast and Fast Mode Plus bus speeds with a 25 MHz system clock. It is a reusable template that was verified on an FPGA with an ESP32-C6 acting as I2C master.
